title: The Counsel of the Elders (Ki Tien Tymmen)
cultural_context: Reflections on ancient proverbs (*Ki Ktien Tymmen*) handed down around the hearth, published in 'Ki Khasi Poems' (1964).

khasi: Ki tien tymmen ba la buh ki kpa,
Ki long kum ki khlur ha ka miet ba dum;
Ki pyni ia ka lynti kaba beit,
Ban lait na ki them ba jylliew;
Ki ong: 'Wat pynjot ia ka burom briew',
'Kamai ia ka hok ba me ieng skhem';
Kine ki ktien ki im ha ka ri,
english: The proverbs bequeathed by the ancient fathers
Are like guiding stars in the pitch-dark night;
They point the direct and righteous path,
Guiding feet away from perilous chasms;
'Earn your living by truth that you may stand firm';
These sacred words live in our motherland,
From primeval antiquity unto this day.

khasi: Wat lehbieit ban klet ia ka niam,
Ia ka tip-kur bad tip-kha ba kyntang;
Uba phai dien na ki kpa tymmen
Un sah khlem jingkyrshan ha ka pyrthei;
Bat skhem ia ki mawbyrsiew jong ka tnum,
Ri ia ka ktien ba pynshai jabiong;
Kine ki ktien tymmen kin long
Ka stieh ba iada ia ka dohnud.
english: Be not foolish to abandon our sacred faith,
Nor forget maternal clan and paternal kin;
He who turns his back on the elders' counsel
Shall find himself forsaken in the wide world;
Hold fast to the hearthstones of your thatched ancestral roof,
Preserve the mother tongue that enlightens the mind;
These proverbs of the elders shall be
The impenetrable shield protecting your soul.
